problem: Learned visual navigation policies are trained in simulation, and existing unsupervised image translation methods (CycleGAN, MUNIT) ignore the policy and optimize photo-realism, so translated images may lose navigation-relevant cues. Direct sim-to-real transfer performs poorly.
motivation: Training RL navigation policies in the real world is infeasible (millions of samples, safety, battery), and paired sim/real data is very expensive to collect. An unsupervised adaptation method needing only a few unpaired target images, and no policy retraining, is therefore valuable.
key_idea: Translate target-domain images into the source domain with a content/style-disentangled translator trained with a policy-based consistency loss, so that the frozen policy's feature extractor gives the same features for different styles of the same content.
insight: Policy-relevant features (obstacles, walls, free space) live in the domain-invariant content, so forcing the frozen policy encoder to be style-invariant preserves them during translation. The ablation without the policy loss (MUNIT-like) drops PointGoal SPL from 0.712 to 0.669 and Explored Ratio from 0.897 to 0.879, and CycleGAN is lower still. This shows that policy-aware translation matters beyond realism.
method: Policy decomposition: the source-domain policy is split into a frozen Policy Feature Extractor F_π (ResNet-18, 128-d representation) and an Action Policy A_π (2-layer GRU) trained with PPO.
Content/style disentanglement: MUNIT-style encoders E^s, E^t map an image to domain-invariant content (128x64x64) and domain-specific style (8-d), and decoders D^s, D^t with AdaIN recombine them.

Policy-based consistency loss: for a target image's content, decode with two styles sampled from N(0,I) into the source domain, and minimize the L1 distance between F_π features of the two decoded images.
Reconstruction and adversarial losses: image and latent reconstruction (weights 10 and 1) plus multi-scale GAN discriminators (weight 1); λ_pol is set to 1 over the mean L1 norm of source features.
Deployment: at test time, target-domain (Replica or real-world) observations are translated to Gibson by PBIT and fed to the unchanged Gibson-trained policy, with no policy retraining.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + 2-layer GRU policy (PPO, frozen at adaptation) + MUNIT-style conv/residual encoder-decoder translator (trained)
setting.training_data: Policy: 72 Gibson training scenes, 30M frames PPO. Translator: 7200 Gibson images, 7200 Replica images (18 scenes), and 1125 real-world images, unpaired, 500K iterations.
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left 10°, turn_right 10°
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson to Replica) plus real world LoCoBot
setting.privileged: none at test time (some unlabeled target-domain images are used for translator training, and 151 real images come from the Seen scene)

numbers.eval_set_note: 900 generated episodes (50 in each of 18 Replica scenes)
numbers.extra: unsupervised adaptation with 7200 unpaired Replica images; policy not retrained

numbers_note: The text says a 70% vs 15% overall success improvement, which conflicts with the table's Overall 77.8% vs 16.7%; table values are reported here. Seen scene: 100% vs 11.1% in the table. Unseen scene: 55.6% vs 22.2% in the table.
results: On Gibson to Replica, PBIT beats CycleGAN (SPL 0.605, Explored Ratio 0.868) and the no-policy-loss ablation (SPL 0.669, Explored Ratio 0.879) on both tasks, and Direct Transfer (SPL 0.505). On a real LoCoBot it reaches 77.8% overall success against 16.7% for Direct Transfer, with 100% in the seen scene and 55.6% in the unseen scene.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is small (18 trials in 2 scenes), and the seen scene shares training images with the translator.
Only geometric tasks (PointGoal, Exploration) with an RGB-only policy are tested; semantic tasks are left as future work.
A separate translator must be trained for each target domain, and text and table numbers are inconsistent in places.
